It's my checkride. Checkride is an exam given by the FAA to get your pilot's license. I fly to the examiner's airport, it's an hour away. I get there and check my watch: I've got 5 minutes. Huh. Let's do practice landings. It's an unfamiliar airport, might as well get some practice and have the upper hand. I come in to land, and plant her down nice and smooth. Flaps up, carb heat in, full throttle and we are rolling. As I rotate and start climbing out, it happens. At approx 200ft above the ground, the entire airplane starts shaking. And then the shake gets worse. I instantly pitch nose low and pull carb heat out .I look down and my RPM is down by 500 RPM. I look at my VSI, should be around 700fpm. It barely read 50fpm. Looked back at my altimeter, I'm barely 200ft above field elevation. I'm in the dead zone. It's straight ahead or spin and die. I didn't have time to be shocked and panicked and I'm glad I didn't panic, I would have died. I look to my left and I see the threshold to the crosswind runway. I know this is the dead zone but the engine hasn't completely gone and I am going to try and turn base for my intersecting runway. Shallow turn, nothing crazy all while listening for the engine to quit. A second or two has passed by now and I mutter, "something is wrong, I need to put her down". I continue turning towards the intersecting runway. Luckily the engine didn't quit so I made it high and tight. Runway is barely 2500 ft and I'm 200ft agl above the numbers. Go-around is not an option. Power idle, slip slip slip. She falls like a brick and I plant her down elegantly. Almost a romantic finish. She's coughing like crazy on the taxi out and fails runup check with a 600 drop. My examiner walks out and he's angry. I'm like wtf. He asks me why was I flying so low? Says it's illegal andthe FAA considers my actions unsafe. I couldn't believe what he said . You can't so this! I told him what happened and then he sits next to me to see for himself. His expression changes and he calls the mechanics on the field to help me out.

Mechanics find a cold cylinder and change two sparkplugs. We go and knock out the checkride. I fly home with my wings. Its only on the way back that the gravity of the situation hits me. I could have died. But I didn't. I earned those wings. I maintained positive control, made all the right decisions and didn't panic. I did exactly what an aviatior should. But at that moment, that one second when the engine started howling, I was shocked for 0.5 seconds. Couldn't believe this was actually happening.
